Every row explains what it does, its starting value and why, and who can change it; Restore recommended works
The eight stored settings that had no screen can be changed and are audited (tests)
Saving from an old page is refused with the conflict message, for rows and sections (test)
Each row shows who changed it last and when; History and Undo work from the row
Search finds rows by name and keyword; old section links land in the right place
ADMIN sees owner-only rows read-only and the server refuses their saves; STAFF never reaches Settings
Axe + 5 sizes, keyboard; ci green at the exact head; every review comment read
gates: AR-1 merged on main (PR #720 in flight at packet time); AR-12 source merged (#693/#695/#702/#716)
invariants: No setting's behaviour changes: same fields, same defaults, same domain writers; this card rebuilds the surface, not the semantics
Every save is audited and carries the revision it read; a stale page is refused with the conflict message, never silently overwritten
Roles are enforced at the server action and DTO boundary: STAFF never reaches Settings; ADMIN sees owner-only rows read-only and their saves are refused server-side
Money stays integer cents; money rows convert dollars to cents at the existing boundary and nowhere else
Feature-detect DEC-1 (Decisions & reviews) rather than hard-depending on its routes; notification preferences stay with AR-13 and are not built here
outcome: Settings becomes one searchable catalog: every BusinessSettings field is a row in one of the nine decided sections (or a panel/link, or listed NOT_A_SETTING with a reason), each row explaining what it does, its starting value and why, and who can change it, with Restore recommended, per-row history and Undo. Every save goes through the setting's existing domain writer or the generic row save on updateBusinessSettings with a per-field stale-page check; no setting's behaviour changes. Section 1 fixes land first: bounded checkUndo, a role check in listSettingsHistory, and removal of the no-revision updateSettingsAction fallback.

risk: Settings writes. The danger is a save path that bypasses a domain writer's side effects or a stale page overwriting a newer value; the spec answers both (existing writers stay authoritative, the generic row save is revision-checked and audited). The catalog touches every settings surface, so the catalog test's field-coverage assertion is the safety net against a silently dropped setting.
